thread:
incident-bot: [ALERT] Canary failure detected for rollout id rl-2026-0315 in eu-west-1. Error rate on gen endpoint > 40% over 2 minutes.
Miguel: ack — I saw the alert, opening thread. Canary was model=redwood/gptx-large@v2026-03-15-weightset-9b.
Miguel: paging James (on-call) for triage, this smells like a weight/tokenizer mismatch.
James (on-call): on it. joining. any customer impact yet?
customer-success-bot: CS: 3 paying customers in eu-west reported corrupted tokens and crashes for short completions. severity: P2 for now, trending up.
Sara: quick check — canary hosts returning lots of "tokenize: illegal byte sequence" in logs. tokenizer version on canary looks like tokenizers:v3 but weightset expects tokenizers:v2. config map might have been overridden during the release.
Lena: Confirmed — rollout manifest had weightset alias 'prod-latest' that points to weightset-9b, but tokenizer_config_ref was left pointing at tokenizers:v3. This would explain decoding mismatches.
Miguel: oof. how many requests hit canary? metrics show burst of 12k requests across canary nodes, lots of 5xx.
James (on-call): immediate mitigation: flip kill-switch flag to stop routing new traffic to the canary. Can someone flip feature flag "new-model-rollout" in prod?
deploy-bot: @James (on-call) received command to toggle flag. Current state: enabled.
ops-runner: flipping flag now -> `POST /api/flags/new-model-rollout {"enabled":false}`
deploy-bot: flag flipped to false. Traffic routing for rollout rl-2026-0315 paused. Verified: no new sessions being routed to canary.
Miguel: good. next: decide rollback vs roll-forward. We have two options: 1) rollback to prod stable weightset (safe), 2) quick roll-forward with corrected tokenizer mapping (faster if confident). Thoughts?
Sara: rollback is safest for customer-facing impact, but rollback will evict the canary and might take ~7m for all nodes. Roll-forward (re-patch tokenizer_config) could be a 2-3m change if we patch the config and reapply the rollout manifest.
James (on-call): given customers already affected and potential for more, prefer rollback to stable for now. Execute conservative path.
Lena: prepping rollback. Model stable alias is prod-stable -> weightset-8b sha:sha8b1234. I'll start a rollback job.
deploy-bot: initiating rollback job rl-2026-0315 -> prod-stable (weightset-8b). Command: `rbctl rollout rollback --id rl-2026-0315 --target-alias prod-stable`
deploy-bot: rollback job started. Progress: 0/12 canary nodes drained.
Miguel: I'll coordinate draining and customers. James, msg CS to inform impacted customers about mitigation.
customer-success-bot: CS note drafted: "We've paused the new model rollout and reverted to the previously stable model. We're continuing to monitor and will update within 30 minutes." QA please confirm before send.
James (on-call): send it. include contact for refunds if customer sees data loss (unlikely).
ops-runner: drain update: 6/12 canary nodes drained, traffic shifted to prod-stable. Error rate dropping back to baseline.
Sara: While rollback is ongoing, capturing postmortem artifacts: diffs of rollout manifest, tokenizer_config refs, and weightset alias histories. Lena, can you dump the alias mapping?
Lena: alias dump attached (short):
```
prod-latest -> weightset-9b (applied 2026-03-15T10:12Z by CI)
prod-stable -> weightset-8b (applied 2026-02-27T23:01Z)
tokenizer-config-ref in manifest -> tokenizers:v3 (unexpected)
```
Miguel: thanks. early hypothesis: CI pipeline step that stitches tokenizer_config into rollout manifest read the wrong branch; config drift allowed tokenizer:v3 to pair with weightset-9b which is incompatible.
James (on-call): action items while rollback completes: 1) Eng-runtime to block autopromote from CI for weightset aliases until validation added (owner: Sara). 2) Infra to add a pre-rollout validation check that ensures tokenizer semantic compatibility (owner: Lena). 3) CS to follow up with impacted customers (owner: customer-success).
Sara: I'll own the validation PR. quick patch idea: validate tokenizer hash matches model tokenizer expectation using `redwoodctl model inspect --weightset weightset-9b --field tokenizer_hash` before allow alias.
Miguel: good. any sign we need a hotfix to production logs or routing?
ops-runner: no hotfix required beyond rollback and flag flip. metrics: 5xxs down to baseline.
deploy-bot: rollback complete. All canary nodes replaced with prod-stable. Health checks green.
James (on-call): great. CS send update to customers. CS: please include ETA for postmortem and offer to join a 1:1 if they want deeper impact analysis.
customer-success-bot: CS update sent. Customers acknowledged and will monitor. No escalations opened.
Miguel: creating incident ticket with timeline + artifacts. Assigning to eng-runtime (Sara) for validation PR and to infra (Lena) for pre-rollout gate.
Sara: starting PR now, will include unit tests and a simple tokenizer-model compatibility check. Target: patch merged within 48h.
Lena: infra will add a pre-rollout admission webhook to CI pipeline. ETA 72h.
James (on-call): closing active mitigation. Please add to postmortem: root cause, detection timeline, mitigation timeline, customer impact, follow-ups.
Miguel: thanks everyone. marking this thread as resolved for now. Will re-open if anything regresses. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: Incident rl-2026-0315 mitigated. Severity downgraded. Follow-up ticket: INC-2026-0315-01 created and assigned."
